lanes.notes: Spawns the byte-exact @xstate/react@6.1.0 suite in a child Vitest run against react@19.2.3, in upstream's own happy-dom environment with globals:true, after re-hashing every vendored byte. The Vitest project executes one wrapper case; the 144 inner upstream identities it certifies are pinned in audit/pristine-runtime.json.

Runs the one-for-one adapted useActor, useActorRef, useSelector, and createActorContext suites on Octane: 75 cases whose names match the pristine lane's identities exactly. Permitted transformations: @testing-library/react to @octanejs/testing-library; `import * as React from 'react'` to 'octane' (namespace-imported base hooks are slotted directly by the compiler); the '../src/index.ts' import root to '@octanejs/xstate'; './utils.tsx' to the adapted './utils.ts' mode helper; explicit describe/it/expect/vi/afterEach imports because the project runs globals:false; the class ErrorBoundary to a @try/@catch component; an explicit `null` dependency array on four deps-less effects, which is Octane's documented spelling of React's run-after-every-render; .tsx to .tsrx. Upstream's `suiteKey === 'strict' ? … : …` expressions are left byte-identical and simply evaluate to the non-strict expectations. Octane-only conformance cases share this Vitest project but sit outside adaptedRoots.tests and are not counted as parity evidence.
Compiles the vendored test/types.test.tsx together with the vendored src using plain tsc against react@19.2.3 and @types/react@19.2.17, reproducing upstream's allowImportingTsExtensions.

Compiles typetests/types.test-d.tsx with tsrx-tsc against the Octane binding. The file is byte-identical to the vendored upstream suite below its header apart from one line (@testing-library/react to @octanejs/testing-library) and is prettier-ignored so that stays verifiable by diff. It is .tsx rather than .tsrx because comments are stripped before TypeScript sees a lowered .tsrx program, so its @ts-expect-error markers would not survive.

Runs one TSRX fixture through this binding on Octane and through the real @xstate/react@6.1.0 on react@19.2.3, asserting byte-identical innerHTML after every click. xstate@5.32.5 is shared by both sides and deliberately not rewritten, so any difference is attributable to the binding.

divergences.upstreamResult: React StrictMode double-invokes render and effects in development, so upstream parametrizes these suites over a strict and a non-strict mode and eight cases branch their render, effect, and observer counts on `suiteKey === 'strict'`.
divergences.octaneResult: Octane has no StrictMode double-invoke, so the adapted helper supplies only the non-strict mode. The eight branching expressions are kept byte-identical and evaluate to upstream's own non-strict expectations; the strict pass is not applicable rather than skipped.
divergences.rationale: StrictMode double-invocation is a React development-mode diagnostic with no Octane counterpart. It is a framework-level absence, not a choice made by this binding.
divergences.consumerImpact: Fewer renders and effect invocations in development than React under StrictMode. Production counts are identical, because React does not double-invoke in production either.
divergences.migrationGuidance: None required. Code that relies on StrictMode to surface impure render logic should keep using React for that diagnostic; Octane never double-invokes.
divergences.reviewCondition: Review if Octane ever adopts a StrictMode-equivalent development double-invoke.

divergences.upstreamResult: Upstream catches an actor's error state with an inline `class ErrorBoundary extends React.Component` using getDerivedStateFromError.
divergences.octaneResult: Octane has no class components, so the adapted fixtures spell the same boundary as a `@try`/`@catch` template block. It catches the same render-phase throw and renders the same data-testid="error" node with the same message, so the assertion is unchanged.
divergences.rationale: Class components are not part of Octane's component model; `@try`/`@catch` is its error-boundary primitive.
divergences.consumerImpact: An application porting a class error boundary must rewrite it as a `@try`/`@catch` block. The caught errors and the recovery behavior are the same.
divergences.migrationGuidance: Replace class error boundaries with a `@try`/`@catch` directive block. Hoist the boundary and its guarded child to module scope and name the child directly in the arm: the arms are hoisted templates and cannot read `props.children`.
divergences.reviewCondition: Review if Octane ever gains class components or a children-transparent boundary component.

ordinaryEvidence.testName: skips the commit-time getSnapshot re-read when a store mutates without notifying between render and commit
ordinaryEvidence.fullName: useSyncExternalStore commit-time re-read skips the commit-time getSnapshot re-read when a store mutates without notifying between render and commit

ordinaryEvidence.testName: reconciles a mutation in the same render-to-commit window when the store notifies, as every xstate actor does
ordinaryEvidence.fullName: useSyncExternalStore commit-time re-read reconciles a mutation in the same render-to-commit window when the store notifies, as every xstate actor does

divergences.upstreamResult: React's useSyncExternalStore re-reads getSnapshot at commit and forces another render when the value moved, so a store mutated between render and commit without notifying is still reconciled into the committed DOM.
divergences.octaneResult: Octane gates its commit-time store sync on the value read during render: an unchanged read enqueues nothing, so a mutation that slips into that window without notifying is not reconciled until the store's next notify. The committed DOM can lag the store by one update in exactly that window.
divergences.rationale: The gate is Octane's runtime design for its own store-sync queue, not a choice made by this binding. The staleness is bounded: the next notify reconciles.
divergences.consumerImpact: Unreachable through this binding. Every xstate actor notifies its observers on transition, and the paired control case shows a notifying mutation reconciles inside the same commit window. Only a hand-rolled store that mutates silently can observe it.
divergences.migrationGuidance: Notify subscribers whenever the snapshot changes, which xstate actors already do. Do not mutate a store's snapshot without emitting.
divergences.reviewCondition: Review if Octane's runtime adopts a commit-time getSnapshot re-read, or if a supported xstate actor ever mutates without notifying.

ordinaryEvidence.testName: renders from getSnapshot on the server when a hand-rolled actor supplies no getServerSnapshot
ordinaryEvidence.fullName: @octanejs/xstate SSR renders from getSnapshot on the server when a hand-rolled actor supplies no getServerSnapshot

ordinaryEvidence.testName: prefers getServerSnapshot over getSnapshot on the server when both are supplied
ordinaryEvidence.fullName: @octanejs/xstate SSR prefers getServerSnapshot over getSnapshot on the server when both are supplied

divergences.upstreamResult: React requires getServerSnapshot for server-rendered content and throws "Missing getServerSnapshot, which is required for server-rendered content" when it is absent, both during server rendering and on the client while hydrating.
divergences.octaneResult: Octane's server hook falls back to getSnapshot when no server snapshot is supplied, so the same component renders instead of throwing. When a server snapshot IS supplied it still wins, so the fallback is a genuine fallback rather than two readers agreeing.
divergences.rationale: Two layers contribute and both are recorded here rather than attributed to the runtime alone. Octane's server runtime defaults the argument, and this port's useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector additionally passes `getServerSelection ?? getSelection` where upstream's use-sync-external-store shim forwards `getServerSelection` unchanged. Upstream's shim is replaced rather than vendored, so this wiring is the port's.
divergences.consumerImpact: Unreachable through the package's public exports: both ported hooks always supply a server snapshot, and useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector is not part of the barrel. Only a hand-rolled actor-like object wired straight to the native hook reaches it, and it renders where React would throw.
divergences.migrationGuidance: Keep supplying getServerSnapshot for anything server-rendered. Code that satisfies React satisfies Octane; the reverse is not guaranteed, so do not rely on the fallback if the same component must also run on React.
divergences.reviewCondition: Review if Octane's server runtime starts requiring getServerSnapshot, or if the port stops defaulting it. The client-hydration half of the same fallback is untested here because this package has no hydration lane; it belongs in packages/octane/tests/hydration/.
